newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was uneven on light to moderate demand and offerings.
The light choice and select spread continues to stretch to a level of

21.40; however, the spread that occurred during this trading period was the smallest seen in the past seven weeks. Retail and HRI demand was mostly for future needs as immediate needs were seasonally light.

The carcass price equivalent index value of a Choice 1-3 550-700 lbs carcass was down .39 at 114.15; 700-850 lbs up .10 at 111.48; Select 1-3 550-700 lbs down .87 at 92.75; 700-850 lbs down .86 at 90.42.

Select and Choice middle meats traded higher with most of the advances early in the trading period. Chuck and round cuts ended the trading period on a weak undertone as processors were forced to control inventories on some of these cuts.

Closely trimmed items traded higher on rather light demand. Trade on beef trimmings were generally steady on light demand and light to moderate offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.70 at 119.96; 700/850 Up 2.19 at 118.29; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.22 at 98.56; 700/850 Up 1.23 at 97.23.

Cow and bull carcass, boneless processing beef, cutter cow cutout - Because of the upcoming holiday-shortened week, many of the fast food suppliers reduced production schedules and grinding requirements for next week. However, there was some interest from the retail grinders.
Therefore, boneless beef traded firm to higher this week on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings.

Additionally, the Utility carcasses were steady, while the Cutter carcass prices were firm on moderate demand and offerings. Furthermore, cow cuts traded at uneven price level, with the Utility cuts being mostly weak and Cutter items trading unevenly steady with a firm undertone noted on some
Utility carcasses steady; Cutter firm; Fresh 90% boneless beef 1.50-2.00 higher; 85% 2.00 higher; 75% steady to weak; 65% 3.00 higher.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, November 21 was estimated at 64.61 per cwt., up .67 from a week ago Friday.
